column1: # The lines of the bash hooks and of the shims, mapped to a hook/ rule ID and the ref it guards ('-'
# for none), or to a notice/ ID and the fields it carries, read by scripts/lib/hook-parity.sh
# (TEST-hook-scenario-parity). One row per line form: an extended regular expression matched against
# the whole line, the ID, and the fields, separated by tabs; a field names the groups of the pattern
# as \1 to \9. A refusal's citation is a field, so that each tree's release is compared.
^pre-commit: refused — the checkout is on 'main', and changes reach main through a pull request \(([^)]+)\)\.
^pre-commit: refused — the checks are red on the resolved merge
^pre-commit: refused — the documentation check is red, and the checks pass before a commit
^pre-commit: refused — the checkout is on the feat/ branch '([^']+)', which carries no merge commit
^pre-merge-commit: refused — the checkout is on 'main', and changes reach main through a pull request \(([^)]+)\)\. git merge --abort, then (merge into|rebase the branch onto) a feat/ branch
^pre-merge-commit: refused — the checkout is on the feat/ branch '([^']+)', which carries no merge commit
^pre-merge-commit: refused — the documentation check is red on the merge
^pre-push: refused — changes reach main through a pull request, not a push \(([^)]+)\)\.
^pre-push: refused — the checks are red, and they pass before anything is pushed

^pre-push: (.+) carries ([0-9]+) draft ADR\(s\); they take their numbers on the branch of the pull request into main, by scripts/ready-for-main\.sh \((README|CONTRIBUTING\.md), Integration branches, step 7\)\.$
^pre-push: the checks passed on this tree before; not run again\.$
^reference-transaction: refused — main moves only to what origin/main has, and changes reach it through a pull request \(([^)]+)\)\. Take up the remote's main: git merge --ff-only origin/main$

^reference-transaction: refused — main moves only to what origin/main has, and changes reach it through a pull request \(([^)]+)\)\. main has commits origin/main lacks; keep them on a branch and take main back: git switch -c feat/<topic> main, then git branch -f main origin/main$
